title: Set up reproducible screenshot pipeline
body:
Two-tier approach from June 2026 research:
- Inline circuit shots: keep each circuit as a .litematic in git (doubles as downloadable course asset); render with the Isometric Renders mod (/isorender area) for transparent-background orthographic PNGs. Technical Utilities mod can render the current Litematica selection directly.
- Hero/chapter shots: Chunky headless. One scene.json per shot committed to git (camera/FOV/chunks); re-shoot after world edits with: chunky -render <scene> -f -reload-chunks.
- Shared post-process script: magick mogrify -trim, pad to consistent aspect, oxipng/pngquant.
Links: https://modrinth.com/mod/isometric-renders https://github.com/chunky-dev/chunky https://modrinth.com/mod/techutils

Bedrock update: Litematica/Isometric Renders/Chunky are all Java-only. But MiEx (bramstout/MiEx) reads BEDROCK worlds natively (1.17+), runs on macOS (Java jar), has a -cli headless mode, exports USD -> Blender Cycles. Studio-grade quality (used for Minecraft Live). Likely unified pipeline: Bedrock world -> MiEx -> Blender with two camera templates (orthographic diagram / cinematic hero), headless via blender -b. Fallback/alt: Chunker CLI (HiveGamesOSS, MIT, headless) converts Bedrock->Java scriptably for any Java-only tool; redstone block states survive conversion (spot-check first run). Avoyd is Windows-only (dead end). Vibrant Visuals shots only possible on an actual Bedrock device, no macOS client.
Links: https://github.com/BramStoutProductions/MiEx https://github.com/HiveGamesOSS/Chunker https://github.com/Moo-Ack-Productions/MCprep https://github.com/Moulberry/Flashback

Revised architecture idea from Fielding: Java server (Fabric) + Geyser/Floodgate, Bedrock world converted once via Chunker. Unlocks: no recurring conversion (Chunky/MiEx read server world dir directly), server-side .schem export via WorldEdit/FAWE (no Java client needed), Carpet+scarpet for automated truth-table verification of circuits + /tick freeze for staging, BlueMap for embeddable interactive 3D views in the Astro site, multiplayer. Caveat: Java server = Java redstone mechanics through the Bedrock client; keep original Bedrock world as Bedrock-mechanics test bed; verify each converted circuit (esp. timing-sensitive Part III builds).

Verified on 7segment. REQUIRED LOCAL PATCH: MiEx exp-23 applyExportSettings has 2 bugs (ExportData.fromJson passes parent JSON to ExportBounds.fromJson instead of entry2; reflection checks Integer/Float/Boolean.isAssignableFrom which never match primitive int/float/boolean fields) - patched classes compiled and jar-updated, stock backup at ~/apps/MiEx/MiEx.jar.orig. Candidate upstream PR. Caveats: MiEx GUI must be closed (LevelDB lock, shots.py checks), Bedrock saves only on world exit (shots.py errors on empty exports).

Renderer feature-complete for course use: --dust solid|power|schematic|realistic (solid default: clean geometric strokes from generated textures in renders/assets/, state-colored shadeless emission, powered glows); --swap old=new block retexturing at render time; --lighting/--transform/--glare/--elevation overrides; scripts/sweep.py style+angle contact sheets. renders/STYLE.md is the style standard (lane color palette TODO for Fielding). Verified on big.usd lab render. Next: angle-sweep Part I builds, fill shots.json, regenerate course images, COMMIT EVERYTHING.

title: Schematic-symbol overlay on CAD aerial render (Tier 1)
body:
Idea from render exploration. The CAD aerial (--technical cad on top view) reads like a PCB layout and is genuinely useful. Next level: overlay standard logic/EE glyphs at component positions, keeping real spatial layout + the extracted dust wire graph:
- redstone torch -> NOT gate (triangle + bubble)
- repeater -> delay/buffer box (show delay ticks)
- comparator -> comparator symbol
- wire tees -> junction dots
We already have component positions (materials) and the wire connection graph (build_vector_wires). Work is drawing/placing glyphs (Blender geometry at world positions facing camera, or PIL compositing at projected screen coords). Solves the 'need a key' problem since symbols are self-explanatory.

NOT doing: Tier 2 (full netlist extraction + re-layout into idealized left-to-right schematic). That's an EDA-grade auto-placement problem; for a course, hand-drawn schematics or the existing Boolean expressions are clearer, and re-layout breaks the spatial correspondence to the build that makes the overlay pedagogically useful.

title: Unified design system across site + Blender schematics + CircuitVerse
body:
Lock ONE visual language across three surfaces so figures and chrome feel consistent.

Canonical palette (single source of truth) drives all three:
- Signal ON = redstone red (site --color-primary oklch(48% 0.18 25)); physically correct AND on-brand. REPLACES CircuitVerse's current lime-green=on.
- Signal OFF = warm grey.
- Accent / logic gates = amber-gold (site --color-accent oklch(78% 0.14 70)); CircuitVerse orange gates already close.
- Backgrounds: warm near-black (dark) / warm paper (light); structure neutrals from site greys.
- Layer height tints (Minecraft renders only): muted earthy per-layer hues, light+dark matched.

Apply to:
1. Site: web/src/styles/global.css :root tokens (currently dark-only, single :root). Fielding leaning toward RESKINNING site to fit the schematics rather than vice versa. Decide dark-only vs light-mode vs light-entirely.
2. Blender renders: scripts/render_usd.py TECHNICAL palettes (already parameterized; mostly done).
3. CircuitVerse: configure a Custom Theme (wire on=red, off=grey, gate=gold, bg) and use for all future captures; re-capture existing *_circuitverse.png for consistency. CircuitVerse supports custom themes (UI theme editor).

KEY semantic decision: ON=red everywhere (kill green=on in CircuitVerse). The green/red conflict is the biggest current inconsistency.
Down-the-road effort; foundation step = author the canonical palette/tokens doc that all three reference.

body: architecture.md section 11 lists 13 decisions. Critical ones: #5 flag-latch timing vs Reg A load (countdown loop correctness), #1 IR/AR never built, #2 Reg B never built, #3 selector encodings. Verify/correct architecture.md from the real machine first, then conform the 12a/12b drafts to it. Blocks line-editing Part III.

Block-level build/verify guide drafted at docs/build-guide-ru-39f8f2.md (uncommitted working doc): builds for IR/AR/RegB/selectors/decoder matrix/HLT latch, strobe delay-ladder timing for Q5+Q11 incl. bench tests, MODE gating spec, countdown acceptance test with failure signatures, and a write-back checklist mapping all 13 open questions to architecture.md sections + drafts.

Testbench milestone 1 PASSED (7/7): Module 10 4-bit repeater-lock register + pulse limiter built programmatically via mineflayer /setblock on the Java-converted RU world (agents-lab server, site 150,60,-396) and verified by automated bot assertions: capture 1011, hold under input change, held-STORE single-capture (limiter), recapture. Harness + README at ~/src/hack/minecraft-agents/tools/ru-testbench/. Key gotcha found: dust bends toward adjacent torches (feed inverter supports via repeater). Scaling to selectors/decoder per docs/build-guide-ru-39f8f2.md is now template work.

In-world build progress (agents-lab server, site 900,60,-396): fetch datapath proven live — IR captures opcode 8 from RAM[0] through MOB->register with T0-phase strobe via pulse limiter. Root-caused and fixed: abandoned seq ring self-latch (ring flattened; phases now bot-driven), stale register-feed row latch, AR lock-bus short into the PC-increment row, missing repeaters on 60-cell runs, ~3200 route cells placed on air past the platform edge (groundpatch). Execute stage: control matrix placed at (-260,-180) + IR->decoder elevated lanes deployed; rails test next. Countdown test (12b.4) still pending.

Session 3 build log (in-world, agents-lab): FETCH STAGE now passes its first full cycle — warm-up PC reset, IR captures RAM[0]=8, PC increments 1,2,3 on phase strobes. Root-caused ~15 distinct hardware bugs: seq-ring self-latch (plot flattened), AR lock-bus short into the PC-increment row, ~3200 circuit cells silently placed on air past the platform edge (groundpatch tool), S3 mux climb columns dropping bridge stones on the RAM address inverters (all-16-rows-select failure), a pcout column self-latching the PC incrementer's carry-in (the +8 counting bug), Paper chunk-ticking requiring forceload (860 chunks), redstone torch burnout from test churn (auto-refresh added to the suite), and an intent-dedup ordering bug that silently reverted repairs. Two bugs remain before the countdown test: a re-latching phantom on the RAM's M3 merge lane (bisected to rows 11-12's span) and the unverified S3-address path for address bit 1. All state, coordinates, and next steps in the project memory + ru-testbench code.

Session 3 final: FETCH DATAPATH COMPLETE — the integrated RU-v1 machine now executes its full fetch sequence with exact data: IR captures opcodes 8 and 9 from RAM[0]/RAM[2], AR captures operands 5 and 1 from RAM[1]/RAM[3], the PC counts and the RAM address tracks it through the S3 mux across all four low addresses. RAM programming verified bit-exact. Suite: 4/5 peak (one deterministic PC-drift anomaly remains: cell2 late-captures the next increment's carry bit ~30s post-strobe — mechanism bisected, fix plan in memory). ~25 hardware root causes found and fixed this session, all synced to code. Next: fix the late-capture, then execute-stage rails (control already deployed), then the countdown acceptance test.

MILESTONE: FETCH SUITE 5/5. The integrated RU-v1 machine in-world now executes complete fetch cycles: PC reset, IR<-RAM[PC] opcode fetch, AR<-RAM[PC] operand fetch, PC increment — all values exact across two full instruction fetches (8,5,9,1 at addresses 0-3). ~30 hardware root causes fixed. Also: /tick rate 100 now used for testing (5x wall-clock speedup, suites ~12 min). Next: execute stage rails, then the countdown acceptance test.

author: claude
body: LDI B blocked on a diagnosed design flaw in the irout (IR->control) routing. After a clean reset of the corrupted irout entry zone, LDI A executes reliably again, but LDI B fails because op9 doesn't decode: IR bit0 never reaches the control decoder. Root cause (driven-feed dump): the four IR-out lanes are pitch-2 (x=-126/-128/-130/-132) and the easternmost (irout0/1, feeding bits 0/1) must cross the others from the west after bridging the arout columns; the descent collides with irout2/irout3's lane stilts in a one-cell-wide gap. Latent until now because the fetch suite never exercises the IR->control path. Fix needs a real routing redesign (documented options A/B/C in the testbench memory; option C -- reroute only b0/b1 around the bundle, keeping turn rows intact -- is lowest risk). Checkpointing here given budget; LDI A milestone stands.

author: claude
body: irout (IR->control) routing fully fixed via lane reorder (laneX=-132+2b, rowZ=-200-2b, offline-validated 0-collision). Both bit0 and bit3 now deliver to the decoder; LDI A passes. The reorder's new b3 path needed several follow-on fixes (feed rep for weak climb, restored a lane rep my heal deleted, healed the descend ground, added descend reps for the longer run). LDI B still fails but now purely on the B-side execute path (SelB spine/ld_b), not decode. Also: LDI/countdown tests need a torch-refresh preamble like the fetch suite.

author: claude
body: Session progress (2026-07-05): irout routing architecturally fixed (lane reorder, offline-validated) -> LDI A executes robustly. LDI B B-side: SelB dip-spine fixed (was reaching only bit3; now all 4 inB ports, tile b0 outputs 15 = AR-bit0 gate fires). Sole remaining LDI B blocker: ld_b strobe -- op9's EX lane isn't firing the ld_b matrix drop (rail-chain rebuild ruled out the chain; each opcode row has its own EX lane, so op8's working ld_a doesn't cover op9's ld_b). Next: with fresh torches (burnout is the top flaky-failure cause), trace op9's EX lane x-230..-215 to find the dead rep, add it. Everything downstream of ld_b is proven, so LDI B should pass once the strobe fires. Full trace + geometry in testbench memory.

author: claude
body: IMPORTANT session-end status (2026-07-05): The irout routing ARCHITECTURE fix is correct and in code (offline-validated reorder), and LDI A executed reliably mid-session. HOWEVER, an air-first bulk consolidation redeploy (to cure accumulated stale-dust states) BACKFIRED: bulk-placing 2813 redstone cells rapidly creates fresh stale-dust states, so LDI A is now regressed (fails post-consolidation even after torch refresh). The world substrate is destabilized. ROOT ISSUE surfaced: a redstone machine this large cannot be reliably deployed/patched via rapid bot setblocks — stale dust and torch burnout make the execute path marginal and inconsistent (probes catch different states). Next session must FIRST build settle-aware deployment tooling (place region -> settle -> cut-and-heal, or structure-then-dust phased), THEN redeploy irout+execC+execD region-by-region, re-verify LDI A, resume LDI B. The logic/code is all correct; the deployment methodology needs to become settle-aware. Full detail in testbench memory.

author: claude
body: RECOVERY EXECUTED TO EXHAUSTION — empirically non-convergent (2026-07-05 20:30). Attempted every in-place repair technique on the regressed irout3 descend: fast cut-and-heal, careful staged heal with settle, turn-corner restore, stale-blocker clearing, and settle-aware per-cell rebuild. NONE converge — each operation breaks a different junction (turn corner read 10->0->10; descend -205 read 9->0 purely from interventions). CONCLUSION: this machine's execute path is too marginal (weak signal levels, dense stale-prone dust, torch burnout) to repair in place via bot commands; the state is chaotic under any touch. Completion requires a fresh effort: (1) CODE ROBUSTNESS PASS -- tighter repeater spacing (~6-8 not 9-15 cells), glitch-filter reps on decode-torch inputs, wider strobe pulses; (2) settle-aware region-by-region FULL redeploy from hardened code; (3) verify fetch 5/5 -> LDI A -> LDI B onward. The architecture/logic are correct and validated in code -- this is purely an engineering-margin + deployment-methodology problem. KEY ORDERING LESSON: harden margins BEFORE deploying; never bulk-redeploy or hand-patch onto an already-marginal substrate. Full detail in testbench memory.

author: claude
body: MILESTONE: LDI B PASSES — both immediate-load instructions now execute end-to-end (LDI A: Reg A=5, LDI B: Reg B=1), and a two-instruction program runs correctly in sequence. Recovered fully from the mid-session regression. Two final bugs found via a per-cell-readback / drive-the-rail-directly technique (much faster than bulk cut-and-heal): (1) a stale blocker stone capping the irout3 descend drop; (2) the ld_b net tapped the rail beside its repeater (repeaters don't emit sideways) — moved the tap to the rail's dust cell. Both fixes in code. STATUS: fetch 5/5, LDI A pass, LDI B pass; full control path proven on both register sides. NEXT: ADD (needs ALU wired: RegA/B->ALU->S1 tiles via SelA1, plus flag latch), then SUB/LDA/LDB/STA/JMP/JIZ/HLT, then countdown.

author: claude
body: HLT (op15) verified: fetch IR=15 -> T2 -> halt_set rail fires. Three instructions now pass end-to-end: LDI A, LDI B, HLT. HLT needed no new datapath (decode->rail only). Remaining for countdown: LDA, JIZ, SUB, STA, JMP. Of these JMP/LDA/STA need new datapath nets (AR->PC, Mem-gate/SelMemAddr, RegA->RAM) but not the ALU; SUB needs the ALU integration and JIZ needs the flag latch (also ALU). ALU integration is the biggest remaining build.

author: claude
body: PIVOT (2026-07-05): per Fielding, stepping back from grinding the bot-built RU-v1 machine (design proven: modules pass, integration validated, 3 instructions ran; blocker was deployment/margin engineering, not correctness). New direction: leverage reference' builds + decide the book's build language. DONE: loaded reference '8-bit computer' world (1.19->1.21.6, at spawn ~x-96..8/y90..112/z2..62, Ben-Eater-style, color-coded sections) into the agents-lab server as world-ref-8bit (RU world preserved, swap via docker-compose LEVEL); exported the full build as FAWE schematic ref-8bit-full.schem (281853 blocks). Build-language recommendation: teach with modular, color-coded, legible per-subsystem builds (ref/Ben-Eater tradition) that map to circuit diagrams and are HAND-buildable (avoids the bulk-deploy stale-dust fragility that plagued the bot build); use spread-out 'see every gate' figures as explanation, compact builds as optimization asides. Server world currently swapped to ref; bots (mindcraft/rp-host) turned off.

author: claude
body: Drafted docs/project-map.md — the full project map tying together: course modules <-> architecture.md sections <-> testbench proofs <-> ref reference exports <-> build language <-> render pipeline. Key structural decisions captured: (1) two-scale color system (STYLE.md wire-role lanes inside components + module-region tints applied only at composition, as a toggleable layer, with a proposed book-wide legend needing Fielding's confirmation); (2) testbench vs canonical builds are distinct artifacts (validate vs teach); (3) testbench campaign RESOLVED architecture open questions Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5 (+partial Q10/Q11) with in-world evidence — flag-timing answer: registers capture on strobe RELEASE, data must outlive strobe; selector encoding answer: one-hot rails + gated-OR, not binary muxes. Roadmap: confirm legend -> flow answers into architecture.md -> carve ref single-component refs -> build canonical module set hand-buildable -> render per module -> optional capstone.

author: claude
body: Architecture write-back complete (step 2 of project-map roadmap): flowed the testbench campaign's empirical findings into architecture.md. RESOLVED with in-world evidence: Q1/Q2 (IR/AR/RegB all built + fetch-verified as Module 10 registers), Q3 for S1/S2 (as-built = one-hot rails + per-source gated-OR merges, NOT binary mux trees — recommend as canonical; S3-S5 still to record), Q5 the critical flag-timing hazard (storage captures on strobe RELEASE; hazard is the data/strobe fall race, not post-writeback re-settle; safe pattern = same-edge LD_A/LD_F with data-fan delay so data outlives strobes). Also added: sequencer STEP-first bring-up note (ring self-latched in integration), countdown sanity-check caveat updated to reflect the resolved timing pattern. Doc keeps its OPEN/RESOLVED marker system; header explains evidence provenance. Unblocks 12a.4/12a.5/12b.2 draft edits per the map.

author: claude
body: Roadmap step 3 done: single-component references carved from reference' build. Method: layer autocorrelation proved his machine is 8 identical bit-slices stacked vertically (adjacent layers 0% similar, period-2 layers 95-98%) — so the 2-layer bit-slice IS the repeating unit; horizontal single-register/word carves are not clean (circuit layers are continuous bus wiring; the wool gaps are framing only). Exported 3 unit references (register bit-slice, RAM bit-plane, ALU bit-slice) + kept the 4 section/full schematics; all 7 now committed-ready in assets/schematics/ref/ with a provenance/credit README including course-use notes (comparator-heavy compact style vs RU-v1 torch/repeater pedagogy = 3b interlude material; vertical vs horizontal scaling contrast; his wool framing = same tint-at-composition philosophy). project-map.md asset table + roadmap updated. Remaining before builds: Fielding confirms the color legend (step 1), then step 4 canonical module builds.
